2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted the original Miscellaneous Case being No.118 of 1988 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for getting the case land pre-empted in the 1st court of the then Munsiff, Kushtia. Subsequently the case was transferred to the court of learned Additional Assistant Judge, Kushtia for disposal and re-numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 1989 contending inter-alia that in the S.A. plot No.749, 27 decimals of land appertaining to S.A. khatian No. 1078 under mouza Baradi originally belonged to one Susanto Kumar Saha who died leaving behind 3(three) brothers Narayan Chandra, Gopal Chandra and Debendra Nath. The aforesaid 3(three) brothers sold the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner on 28.08.1988. The further case of the pre-emptor is such that he is a contiguous land holder of the case plots No.749, 750 and 750/1999. The pre-emptor is the owner of some land in plot No.750 and 750/1999. The case land is outside of municipality and it is a "Bhita" with cultivable land. The purchaser-pre-emptee is a stranger. For the requirement of the pre-emptor knowing about the case kabla he instituted the original case within time for getting the case land pre-empted. 

 3. The contrary case of the purchaser-pre-emptee in short is thus that the case land is not the agricultural land and that the case is bad for defect of parties and not maintainable. The further case of the pre-emptee is such that he is a contiguous land-holder of the case land and the land appertaining to C.S. khatian No.1078 in plot No.749 in fact originally belonged to one Susanto Kumar who died leaving, three brothers namely Narayan Chandra, Gopal Chandra and Deben Chandra. The three brothers for want of money wanted to sale the property and executed a bainanama in favour of the pre-emptets-petitioner on 02.03.1965. Subsequently they migrated to India. Thereafter the pre-emptee-petitioner Lutfor Rahman filed a Title Suit being No.30 of 1977 in the 1st Court of the then munsiff, Kushtia for Specific Performance of Contract for getting a registered sale deed. The pre-emptee-pettlioner obtained the decree and through Execution Case he obtained the registered sale deed in his favour which is within the knowledge of the pre-emptor. The pre-emptee-petitioner after his bainapatra constructed his homestead in the case land and planted various trees with an expenditure of Tk.2,84,000/-(two lac eighty four thousand). The pre-emptee-purchaser thus have become the owner of some land of case plot No.750 and 750/1999 and as such he is a contiguous land owner of the case land. The case land as is situated in plot No.749 is a non-agricultural land which is not pre-emptable under section 96 of the State Acquisition And Tenancy Act, 1950. As because; the pre-emptee is a contiguous land owner of the case land, the original case is not maintainable. 

 12. On perusal of the case records it transpires that admittedly the case land measuring an area of 27 decimals of land in S.A. plot No.749 of khatian No.1078 appertaining to mouza Baradi belonged to the predecessor of the vendors Susanto Kumar Saha. It is also admitted that Susanto died leaving behind three brothers namely Narayan, Gopal and Debendra. These three brothers transferred the case land in favour of the pre-emptee-petitioner by way of a bainapatra on 02.03.1965. Thereafter without execution and registration of the kabla deed while they left this county the pre-emptee-purchaser instituted a suit for Specific Performance of Contract being Title Suit No. 30 of 1977 and in that suit he has obtained a decree and by its execution the kabla deed was registered through court. It is not denied from any corner that the case land after acquisition by way of purchase was developed and the purchaser constructing the pucca homestead started to reside therein. Therefore obviously the case land is being used by the purchaser-pre-emptee-petitioner as his homestead. 

 13. Having gone through the evidence on record I find that the purchaser-pre-emptee is the owner of some land of case plot No.750 and 750/1999. The case land consists of three plots which are 749, 750, 750/1999. From the C.S. khatians being No.653, 654 and 655 corresponding to S.A. khatian No. 562 it appears that the nature of the case land is homestead. The said khatians makes it clear that from the very beginning the land in dispute is being used as homestead. Furthermore, I have come across from the case records that the learned trial court during disposal of the original suit adverting evidence held that the purchaser-pre-emptee is a contiguous land owner of the case land and he has 11½ decimals of land in plot No.750 and 750/1999 and the pre-emptor as P.W.1 admitted in his deposition that the purchaser-petitioner along with one Suresh Chandra acquired the land of plot No.750 and 750/1999. The pre-emptor subsequently claiming the land of two plots 750 and 750/1999 filed a suit being No.161 of 1970 against the pre-emptee and one Suresh Chandra but failed to succeed. In this way it is obvious from the case records that the learned appellate court without rebutting the findings of the trial court on this very particular pertinent point adverting the evidence on records decided the merit of the appeal.
